main_text.l: On fine admiratione quâdam (Alma Mater !) obleruavit vir multis nominibus illustris, rara videri vestigia te retrorsum fuisse spectantia, cùm infinita à te promota sint. Itâ sanè res habet; innumeri sunt, qui eruditionem suam Tibi acceptam ferre debent; pauci autem, qui eruditionis suæ monumentis Tibi dedicandis id testatum faciunt. Cùm igitur de Annotationum mearum dedicatione non nemo mecum ageret, Tui statim animum meum subiit cogitatio, nec (quod hanc rem attinet) quicquam mihi prius aut antiquius fuit, quàm ut hæ Laborum meorum primitiæ sub Tuo nomine in lucem
[Remainder of the page is badly show-through damaged; the faint text beneath the main column is not transcribed.]

marginalia.note: Verulam. Sapient. Vet. in Epist. Dedicat. ad Acad. Cantab.

page.notes: The first lines of the body are partly obscured by show-through from the reverse page; the readings of "Ore" and the line "rara videri vestigia te retrorsum fuisse" are doubtful. The marginal note text at the right is small and partly faint. The text of the initial letter is a woodcut "N", read here as the opening "On" of a word; the first letter is uncertain. Words in the middle of the text (e.g. "Vestigia", "promota") are doubtful and should be checked against the scan. The page is heavily degraded; the lower lines below "lucem" are not legible enough to transcribe.
